title: The Challenge of Telework During COVID-19 with Kristen Shockley, PhD

sentences.en: Millions of Americans who once spent their days in offices are now entering their fourth
sentences.zh: 数百万曾经整天待在办公室里的美国人，如今迎来了全职远程办公的第四个月

sentences.en: month of full-time telework, commuting to their new desks in their basements or corners of living
sentences.zh: 他们把通勤改到了地下室或客厅角落的新书桌前

sentences.en: rooms, often while also trying to take care of children whose schools, summer camps and daycares are closed.
sentences.zh: 通常还得一边照顾那些学校、夏令营和日托中心都已关闭的孩子。

sentences.en: Other workers, meanwhile, are outfitting themselves with masks and hand sanitizer and cautiously returning to their long empty cubicles.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，其他员工则戴上口罩和免洗手液，小心翼翼地回到长期空置的隔间里。

sentences.en: In addition to being a public health crisis, the COVID-19 pandemic has proven to be a forced, unplanned experiment in mass telework and work-family conflict.
sentences.zh: 除了是一场公共卫生危机，新冠疫情还被证明是一场被迫的、未经计划的关于大规模远程办公和工作与家庭冲突的实验。

sentences.en: How is it turning out for American office workers?
sentences.zh: 这对美国办公室职员来说结果如何？

sentences.en: Have we been more or less productive?
sentences.zh: 我们的生产力是提高了还是降低了？

sentences.en: And what might be the effects on the future of work?
sentences.zh: 它又可能对未来的工作产生什么影响？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》

sentences.en: Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association.
sentences.zh: 美国心理学协会的旗舰播客。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: Our guest today is Dr. Kristen Shockley, an Associate Professor of Psychology at the University of
sentences.zh: 我们今天的嘉宾是佐治亚大学的心理学副教授

sentences.en: Georgia.
sentences.zh: 克里斯滕·肖克利博士。

sentences.en: Dr. Shockley has spent her career studying the intersection of work and family life.
sentences.zh: 肖克利博士的整个职业生涯都在研究工作与家庭生活的交集。

sentences.en: She's conducted research on how employees balance work and family demands, how work-family conflict
sentences.zh: 她开展了关于员工如何平衡工作与家庭需求的研究，研究工作与家庭的冲突

sentences.en: affects people's health, and how dual-career couples navigate work and family roles.
sentences.zh: 如何影响人们的健康，以及双职工夫妻如何平衡工作与家庭角色。

sentences.en: When the COVID-19 crisis hit, she realized that the upheaval caused by school and office closures made those questions
sentences.zh: 当新冠危机爆发时，她意识到学校和办公室关闭所引起的巨变，使得这些问题

sentences.en: even more pressing, and she set out to investigate how workers are adjusting.
sentences.zh: 变得更加紧迫，于是她着手调查员工们是如何适应的。

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到《心理学谈话》

sentences.en: Psychology, Dr. Shockley.
sentences.zh: 肖克利博士。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: You received a rapid response grant from the
sentences.zh: 您获得了

sentences.en: National Science Foundation to look at how workers are coping with the abrupt transition to telework during the COVID-19 shutdowns.
sentences.zh: 国家科学基金会的快速反应资助，以研究工人在新冠疫情停摆期间如何应对向远程办公的突然过渡。

sentences.en: Can you talk about why you thought it was important to do this research now, how you're doing it, and what questions are you asking?
sentences.zh: 您能谈谈为什么您认为现在做这项研究很重要、您是怎么做的、以及您都在问哪些问题吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so when, I think it was March 13th, when we started realizing that a lot of people were going to be transitioning to remote work,
sentences.zh: 是的，所以当，我想是3月13日，当我们开始意识到很多人将要过渡到远程工作时

sentences.en: I contacted one of my longtime collaborators at the University of South Florida, Tammy Allen, and said, should we try to get a rapid grant to study this?
sentences.zh: 我联系了我在南佛罗里达大学的长期合作者之一塔米·艾伦，说，我们要不要试着申请一个快速资助来研究这个？

sentences.en: Just because this is sort of a natural experiment like we've never seen before with so many people moving into remote work.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为这是一种我们从未见过的自然实验，有这么多人转向了远程工作。

sentences.en: So we proposed a study to the
sentences.zh: 所以我们向

sentences.en: National Science Foundation, and I think we wrote it up within eight days and heard back seven days later that it was funded.
sentences.zh: 国家科学基金会提交了一项研究提案，我想我们在八天内就写好了，七天后就收到了获得资助的回复。

sentences.en: So the whole process has been very rapid.
sentences.zh: 所以整个过程非常迅速。

sentences.en: And we set out really to explore
sentences.zh: 而我们着手真正探讨的是

sentences.en: best practices in remote work, because there's been a good amount of research on it.
sentences.zh: 远程工作的最佳实践，因为之前已经有相当数量关于它的研究。

sentences.en: But it's largely
sentences.zh: 但它在很大程度上是

sentences.en: cross-sectional data comparing non-telecommuters to telecommuters.
sentences.zh: 将非远程办公者与远程办公者进行比较的横断面数据。

sentences.en: So what we wanted to dig into is within a sample of people who are all telecommuting, where you don't have some of these selection
sentences.zh: 所以我们想要深入研究的是，在一群都在远程办公的人群中，在这里你不会遇到其中一些选择

sentences.en: effects, like managers picking people they want to telecommute.
sentences.zh: 效应，比如管理者挑选他们想要远程办公的人。

sentences.en: When everybody's in the kind of same situation, what are factors that vary day-to-day that might impact people's well-being as well as their productivity?
sentences.zh: 当每个人都处于同一种情况时，那些日常变化的、可能会影响人们福祉以及生产力的因素有哪些？

sentences.en: So we just thought it was really just an unprecedented time to study these important issues and then be able to say, we have some evidence-based recommendations moving forward to
sentences.zh: 所以我们只是觉得这是一个研究这些重要问题的空前绝后的时期，然后能够说，我们有一些循证建议可以向前推进

sentences.en: disseminate broadly.
sentences.zh: 并广泛传播。

sentences.en: Do you have any results yet that you could talk about?
sentences.zh: 您现在有什么可以谈论的研究结果吗？

sentences.en: So we just wrapped data collection up on Saturday.
sentences.zh: 我们刚在周六结束了数据收集。

sentences.en: So we haven't analyzed anything formally.
sentences.zh: 所以我们还没有正式分析任何东西。

sentences.en: I did dig into the data a little bit just to look at some descriptive things.
sentences.zh: 我确实稍微深入了一下数据，只是看了一些描述性的东西。

sentences.en: A few of the interesting things I saw where we asked people, and I should say the entire sample is they're all working fully
sentences.zh: 我看到的一些有趣的事情是，我们问了人们，我应该说整个样本都是完全在

sentences.en: remote, but we're not working remote very much at all, 10% or less before COVID.
sentences.zh: 远程工作，但在新冠之前他们几乎根本不远程工作，占10%或更少。

sentences.en: So we asked them, while COVID remains a public health threat, and what percent of the time would you want to stay working remote?
sentences.zh: 所以我们问他们，在新冠仍然是公共卫生威胁的情况下，你希望有多大比例的时间继续远程工作？

sentences.en: And the vast majority said 100%.
sentences.zh: 绝大多数人回答100%。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think it was 90% of the samples said 100%.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为90%的样本都回答了100%。

sentences.en: That's pretty amazing.
sentences.zh: 这真是太惊人了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That speaks to the fact that people are saying, you know, I don't want the risk.
sentences.zh: 这说明了这样一个事实，人们在说，你知道，我不想冒风险。

sentences.en: And even if this arrangement's not perfect, it's worth it to not, you know, expose, have potential exposure.
sentences.zh: 即使这种安排并不完美，为了不，你知道，暴露于潜在的暴露风险中，这也是值得的。

sentences.en: We also asked once COVID is no longer as big of a threat, what percentage of the time would you like to work remote?
sentences.zh: 我们还询问了，一旦新冠不再是那么大的威胁，你希望有多大比例的时间远程工作？

sentences.en: And there we saw a very spread out distribution.
sentences.zh: 在那里我们看到了一个非常分散的分布。

sentences.en: So the most common responses were a hundred and zero, but then it was really spread out, really spread out in between.
sentences.zh: 所以最常见的回答是一百和零，但随后它真的很分散，中间分布得很广。

sentences.en: And the average was 46%.
sentences.zh: 而平均值是46%。

sentences.en: Huh?
sentences.zh: 哈？

sentences.en: What that's telling me is, you know, some people are liking it.
sentences.zh: 这告诉我的是，你知道，有些人喜欢它。

sentences.en: Some aren't.
sentences.zh: 有些人不喜欢。

sentences.en: I think for most people, they're seeing working remote, some at the time would be nice, but this 100%, you know, has some
sentences.zh: 我认为对大多数人来说，他们认为有一部分时间远程工作会很好，但这个100%，你知道，有一些

sentences.en: downsides, probably largely in terms of, you know, social isolation, not feeling like you get out of the house ever.
sentences.zh: 缺点，可能主要在于，你知道，社交隔离，感觉自己永远不会出门。

sentences.en: So let's shift gears for a minute to talk about telework more broadly.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们换个话题，谈谈更广泛意义上的远程工作。

sentences.en: Even before the pandemic, more than 26 million Americans were working remotely, at least part of the time, which is about 16% of the total US labor force of 165 million.
sentences.zh: 甚至在大流行之前，就有超过2600万美国人至少有一部分时间在远程工作，这约占总数1.65亿的美国劳动力队伍的16%。

sentences.en: How well was that working?
sentences.zh: 那之前运作得怎么样？

sentences.en: There's kind of an idea in the popular imagination that people slack off and they're less productive when they telework.
sentences.zh: 大众想象中有一种观点认为，人们在远程工作时会偷懒，生产力会下降。

sentences.en: Does the research back that up?
sentences.zh: 研究支持这一点吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, there is that huge perception.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实有这种巨大的看法。

sentences.en: And we look at the headlines are kind of all over the place with, is teleworking a good or a bad thing, you know, pre-COVID?
sentences.zh: 我们看到头条新闻形形色色，关于远程工作是一件好事还是一件坏事，你知道，在新冠之前？

sentences.en: And actually the data
sentences.zh: 而实际上数据

sentences.en: really don't suggest that people typically slack off.
sentences.zh: 并没有真正表明人们通常会偷懒。

sentences.en: If anything, they show that people are the same or more productive.
sentences.zh: 如果有的话，它们表明人们的生产力保持不变甚至更高。

sentences.en: We don't have a lot of good experiments, you know, which is the best way to really disentangle.
sentences.zh: 我们没有很多好的实验，你知道，这是真正厘清的最佳方法。

sentences.en: Is it teleworking that's causing you to be more or less productive?
sentences.zh: 是远程工作导致你的生产力更高还是更低？

sentences.en: But there was one really solid experiment out there and they found it was in a call center and they found
sentences.zh: 但确实有一个非常扎实的实验，他们发现在一个呼叫中心，他们发现

sentences.en: that the workers who worked from home made significantly more calls every day.
sentences.zh: 在家工作的员工每天打的电话明显更多。

sentences.en: They actually worked longer hours, but the quality of their calls were just as high as they were before.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上工作了更长时间，但他们电话的质量和以前一样高。

sentences.en: So suggesting people are more efficient, I think, from home, which is in a lot of cases, I would say largely because you're not
sentences.zh: 所以这表明人们在家时效率更高，我认为，在很多情况下，我可以说很大程度上是因为你没有

sentences.en: being interrupted, you know, by coworkers and the noisy environment of the office.
sentences.zh: 被同事打扰，也没有办公室嘈杂的环境。

sentences.en: Now, of course,
sentences.zh: 现在，当然

sentences.en: COVID is a little bit different because people have kids at home.
sentences.zh: 新冠有点不同，因为人们家里有孩子。

sentences.en: So they may have interruptions if they wouldn't under a normal remote work arrangement where they would have childcare.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果是在他们有托儿服务的正常远程工作安排下不会遇到的话，他们可能会受到打扰。

sentences.en: Before the COVID-19 pandemic, some early adopters, including Best Buy, IBM and Yahoo, were reversing policies that allowed employees to telecommute.
sentences.zh: 在COVID-19大流行之前，一些早期采用者，包括百思买、IBM和雅虎，正在撤销允许员工远程办公的政策。

sentences.en: They cited leadership changes and a growing need for a creative collaboration.
sentences.zh: 他们列举了领导层的变化以及对创造性协作不断增长的需求。

sentences.en: Do you think that these companies will continue on that path once the emergency is over?
sentences.zh: 您认为这些公司在紧急状态结束后会继续沿着这条路走下去吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, those are really interesting, especially Best Buy, because they had been really progressive, actually, in allowing people to work however or wherever.
sentences.zh: 是的，那些真的很有趣，特别是百思买，因为他们实际上非常激进，允许人们以任何方式或在任何地方工作。

sentences.en: And then I was surprised to see them roll that back because the data actually, at least the data that was published, suggested that was working.
sentences.zh: 然后我很惊讶地看到他们取消了这一政策，因为数据，至少是已发表的数据，表明这很有效。

sentences.en: But I think moving forward, based on what I'm seeing just in informal discussions as well as in
sentences.zh: 但我认为展望未来，根据我从非正式讨论以及

sentences.en: headlines, I think a lot of companies are going to become much more open to remote work.
sentences.zh: 头条新闻中看到的情况，我认为许多公司将对远程工作变得更加开放。

sentences.en: I think it's going to be important for recruitment and retaining people in the workforce now that a lot of people have gotten a taste for it.
sentences.zh: 我认为，既然很多人已经尝到了甜头，这对于在劳动力队伍中招聘和留住人才将是很重要的。

sentences.en: I think a lot of employees are going to sort of demand it and want a workforce to allow that.
sentences.zh: 我认为很多员工会有点要求它，并希望有一个劳动力队伍来允许这样做。

sentences.en: And there's also a lot of benefits from a cost-saving standpoint.
sentences.zh: 而且从节省成本的角度来看，也有很多好处。

sentences.en: You don't have to have as much office space so you can save on real estate.
sentences.zh: 你不必拥有那么多的办公空间，所以你可以节省房地产开支。

sentences.en: And you can also, if you have a fully remote workforce, you can recruit from anywhere in the world, which really puts you in advantage, you know, in trying to get top talent.
sentences.zh: 而且你还可以，如果你拥有完全远程的劳动力队伍，你可以在世界任何地方招聘，这确实让你在争取顶尖人才时占据优势。

sentences.en: So I'm projecting, you know, there's no way really to know, but I think we will see more of a shift to remote work moving forward.
sentences.zh: 所以我预测，你知道，真的没有办法知道，但我认为我们未来会看到更多向远程工作的转变。

sentences.en: Is teleworking equally good for everyone?
sentences.zh: 远程工作对每个人都同样好吗？

sentences.en: Is there some kind of a profile of the person who thrives and the person who really struggles?
sentences.zh: 是否存在某种类型的画像，即谁能蓬勃发展，谁又会真正挣扎？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个很好的问题。

sentences.en: And that was one of the things we're trying to uncover in our grant, in our rapid grant, because there's hardly any research out there at all on the topic.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们在我们的资助、在我们的快速资助中试图揭开的事情之一，因为关于这个主题几乎没有任何研究。

sentences.en: I think there's one study that looked at personality.
sentences.zh: 我想有一项研究考察了人格。

sentences.en: But other than that, there's a lot to be done.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，还有很多工作要做。

sentences.en: So we were exploring different personality variables in our data set.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在我们的数据集中探索不同的人格变量。

sentences.en: We're also exploring things like family structure, the way that you like to manage work and family.
sentences.zh: 我们还在探索诸如家庭结构、你喜欢管理工作和家庭的方式等事情。

sentences.en: Because if you're someone who really likes to keep them separate, obviously working from home does not allow you to do that.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你是一个真的很喜欢把它们分开的人，显然在家工作不允许你这样做。

sentences.en: So we're predicting it's going to be more of a challenge for people like that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们预测对这样的人来说这将是一个更大的挑战。

sentences.en: We're also exploring aspects of the physical office at home.
sentences.zh: 我们还在探索家中物理办公室的各个方面。

sentences.en: I think that makes a really big difference in how well and comfortable people are telecommuting.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对于人们远程办公的效果和舒适度有着非常大的影响。

sentences.en: You know, if you have a setup where your chair is not quite right, you don't have the multiple monitors, you're just not comfortable.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你有一个设置，你的椅子不太对，你没有多个显示器，你就是不舒服。

sentences.en: And I think it's hard to be productive and enjoy teleworking in that arrangement.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为在这种安排下很难保持高产并享受远程工作。

sentences.en: So there's some basic ideas out there in the literature, but that's something we're hoping to really hone in on with this new data.
sentences.zh: 所以文献中存在一些基本的想法，但这正是我们希望通过这些新数据真正深入探讨的事情。

sentences.en: I remember hiring my first teleworking staffer more than 15 years ago, and the only ways we could stay connected were by email and the telephone.
sentences.zh: 我记得在15年前多以前雇佣我的第一个远程办公员工时，我们保持联系的唯一方式是通过电子邮件和电话。

sentences.en: But now there are applications like Teams and Google
sentences.zh: 但现在有了诸如Teams和Google

sentences.en: Hangouts and Zoom.
sentences.zh: Hangouts以及Zoom之类的应用程序。

sentences.en: Was telework already on the upswing before the pandemic, notwithstanding the rollbacks that I mentioned just a minute ago?
sentences.zh: 抛开我刚刚提到的那些政策倒退不谈，在疫情爆发之前，远程工作就已经在上升了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it seems to be that the trend is, you know, more and more people teleworking and
sentences.zh: 所以看来趋势是，你知道，越来越多的人远程办公，并且

sentences.en: people starting to take advantage of some of these technologies you're talking about.
sentences.zh: 人们开始利用你所说的其中一些技术。

sentences.en: And what the academic literature was suggesting pre-COVID was it's best to use the most, what they call high fidelity technology that you can use.
sentences.zh: 而学术文献在新冠之前所表明的是，最好使用他们所谓的你能使用的保真度最高的技术。

sentences.en: So that would be, you know, use Zoom or Skype or Teams over the phone, because when you see people face-to-face or not, I guess not face-to-face,
sentences.zh: 所以那将是，你知道，使用Zoom、Skype或Teams而不是电话，因为当你面对面看到人或者不，我想不是面对面

sentences.en: but when you can see people's face while you're speaking, you know, that's supposed to mimic more of a face-to-face interaction.
sentences.zh: 但是当你说话时能看到人们的脸，你知道，这应该是为了模仿更多的面对面互动。

sentences.en: And so that was sort of the, the common advice that I had been giving to people.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是，我一直给人们的常见建议。

sentences.en: But what's been interesting during the pandemic is this concept of Zoom fatigue.
sentences.zh: 但在大流行期间有趣的是这个Zoom疲劳的概念。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, a lot of discussion about it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有很多关于它的讨论。

sentences.en: I'm experiencing it myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己也在经历它。

sentences.en: So that's, that had not been researched at all.
sentences.zh: 所以那是，这根本没有被研究过。

sentences.en: So that's something else that we're exploring in, in our grant, because we have daily
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们在我们的资助中正在探索的另一件事，因为我们有每日

sentences.en: reports of what technology people use and how much during, you know, how frequently they use the different technologies throughout each day.
sentences.zh: 报告，关于人们使用什么技术以及使用多少，你知道，在每一天中他们使用不同技术的频率如何。

sentences.en: So we're going to try to predict sort of what's the optimal level of using these technologies, because I think in some cases they're really useful, but

sentences.en: maybe we were starting to overuse them when things could have just been a quick phone call and we started relying on, on Zoom or TeaMs.
sentences.zh: 也许我们开始过度使用它们，而本来只需一个简短的电话，我们就开始依赖Zoom或Teams。

sentences.en: That's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 看看那里会产出什么将会很有趣。

sentences.en: In a recent review of the research, you talked about how some people are segmenters and others are blenders and that segmenters may find remote work more difficult.
sentences.zh: 在最近对研究的综述中，你谈到了有些人是划分者，而另一些人是融合者，划分者可能会发现远程工作更加困难。

sentences.en: Can, can you explain what that all means?
sentences.zh: 能，你能解释一下这一切意味着什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So that's the concept of boundary management strategies.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是边界管理策略的概念。

sentences.en: So individuals exist on this continuum.
sentences.zh: 因此，个人存在于这个连续体上。

sentences.en: So at one end, you have the segmenters and these are the people who really like to keep work and family separate.
sentences.zh: 所以在另一端，你有划分者，这些人真的很喜欢把工作和家庭分开。

sentences.en: So they're not talking about work when they get home.
sentences.zh: 所以他们回家时不谈论工作。

sentences.en: They're not talking about their personal life at work.
sentences.zh: 他们在工作时不谈论他们的个人生活。

sentences.en: They're not going to have pictures on their desk at work.
sentences.zh: 他们不会在工作桌上放照片。

sentences.en: They're just really think of them as two separate domains.
sentences.zh: 他们只是真的把它们看作两个独立的领域。

sentences.en: And then the other end, you have the integrators and they're the exact opposite.
sentences.zh: 然后在另一端，你有整合者，他们完全相反。

sentences.en: You know, they're the people that are constantly while at work, juggling things from home.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们是在工作时不断兼顾家庭事务的人。

sentences.en: They might get home and be really likely to work later in the evening, checking emails all the time.
sentences.zh: 他们回到家可能很可能会在傍晚晚些时候工作，一直在检查电子邮件。

sentences.en: And so it's just really a personal preference of what strategy people works best for them to manage work and family.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是一种个人偏好，关于什么策略对他们管理工作和家庭效果最好。

sentences.en: So when you're working from home, then you have this added challenge of, if you're a segmenter,
sentences.zh: 所以当你在家工作时，你就有了一个额外的挑战，如果你是一个划分者

sentences.en: it's really hard to keep those things separate when they're occurring in the same location.
sentences.zh: 当这些事情发生在同一个地点时，要保持这些事情分开真的很难。

sentences.en: So advice we give to people in that situation is try to have a separate room that's really designated as your workspace that's only used for that.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们针对处于这种状况的人给出的建议是：尽量设一个独立的房间，专门用作工作区，只用来办公。

sentences.en: And it's, which, you know, is easier said than done depending on where you live and the kind of space you have.
sentences.zh: 这说起来容易做起来难，具体要看你住在哪里以及你有什么样的空间。

sentences.en: But that's the ideal situation and to have a door so that you can close that.
sentences.zh: 但这是最理想的情况，而且最好带一扇门，这样你就可以把门关上。

sentences.en: So your family members know, okay, when that door is closed, that means this person is, I have to think of them as not here.
sentences.zh: 这样你的家人就会知道，好吧，当那门关着的时候，就意味着这个人，我得把他们当成不在家。

sentences.en: So those are some kind of tricks to try to make it feel more segmented.
sentences.zh: 所以这些是一些小技巧，试图让它感觉更有界限感。

sentences.en: What about differences between managers and line employees when it comes to teleworking?
sentences.zh: 那么，在远程办公方面，经理和基层员工有什么区别呢？

sentences.en: Is it, is it harder to be a remote manager?
sentences.zh: 做远程经理是不是更难？

sentences.en: And how do employees react to having a boss who teleworks?
sentences.zh: 员工对有一个远程办公的老板有什么反应？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's another thing where there's not very much research on the topic at all.
sentences.zh: 对，这是另一个几乎没有什么相关研究的课题。

sentences.en: There's one study about bosses who telework and comparing them, their relationship with their subordinates who are in office and their subordinates who are also teleworking.
sentences.zh: 有一项研究是关于远程办公的老板的，他们对比了老板与在办公室的下属以及同样在远程办公的下属之间的关系。

sentences.en: And the other comparison is managers who are in the office.
sentences.zh: 另一个对比对象是在办公室办公的经理。

sentences.en: So you have kind of these four different quadrants and not surprisingly that the relationships are a bit more strained with the managers who are working remote.
sentences.zh: 所以你有这四种不同的象限，毫无意外，远程办公经理的上下级关系会稍微紧张一些。

sentences.en: They don't explore why, but my hypothesis would be if they're just not having as many interactions
sentences.zh: 他们没有探讨原因，但我的假设是，如果他们只是互动没有那么多的话，

sentences.en: with people, you're not, you don't have the chance just when you're walking by someone to kind of have that informal back and forth in the hallways.
sentences.zh: 跟其他人比，你不会在走过某人身边时，顺便在走廊里进行那种非正式的交流。

sentences.en: So I think there are some challenges there.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这其中存在一些挑战。

sentences.en: And another thing we set out, set out to explore in the grant was what are actually the best practices for managers who are telecommuting?
sentences.zh: 我们在这次资助中着手探讨的另一件事是，对于远程办公的经理来说，真正的最佳实践是什么？

sentences.en: Cause there's, there's a lot of theoretical discussion of that sort of ideas put forth in the academic literature, but we don't have a lot of actual data to back it up.
sentences.zh: 因为在学术文献中有很多关于这类想法的理论讨论，但我们没有很多实际数据来支持它。

sentences.en: So that was something that was a core part of our study was to say, well, you know, what kind of
sentences.zh: 所以这是我们研究的核心部分，就是去探讨，你知道，什么样的

sentences.en: things are managers doing on a daily basis when people are having a good day and what kind of things are they doing that sort of contribute to people not having a great day?
sentences.zh: 事情是经理们在人们状态好时日常在做的，又是什么样的事情在某种程度上导致了人们状态不好？

sentences.en: Um, so that's another question, which I hope to have data to be able to speak more directly to it in the future.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以这是另一个问题，我希望将来能有数据来更直接地说明这一点。

sentences.en: A lot of questions out there.
sentences.zh: 有很多这样的问题。

sentences.en: There really are.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And that's really why we did this grant.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们申请这笔资金的原因。

sentences.en: Cause it's just amazing how little we have actual empirical evidence for the American Psychological Association conducted a
sentences.zh: 因为令人惊奇的是，我们几乎没有什么实证依据。美国心理协会在上个月进行了一项

sentences.en: stress in America survey last month that found nearly half of parents with children under age 18
sentences.zh: 名为“美国压力”的调查，发现近一半家里有18岁以下孩子的父母

sentences.en: at home said their stress levels related to the coronavirus pandemic were high with managing the kids online learning, a significant source of stress for many.
sentences.zh: 表示，他们与新冠疫情相关的压力水平很高，其中管理孩子的在线学习是许多人压力的一个重要来源。

sentences.en: What can people do to make this work life family balancing act easier?
sentences.zh: 人们能做些什么来让这种工作、生活和家庭的平衡更容易一些呢？

sentences.en: I feel like that's a million dollar question right now, right?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这现在是个价值百万美元的问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, it's such an unprecedented thing because most of what we know about teleworking comes from
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一件前所未有的事情，因为我们对远程办公的大多数了解都来自于

sentences.zh: 假设人们在工作期间，孩子都在学校或有托儿服务。

sentences.zh: 双职工并且继续工作的夫妇那里收集了数据，但他们家里有年幼的孩子，而且他们的托儿服务，嗯，无论是日托还是保姆都不再来了。

sentences.en: Um, and we were exploring what are people doing?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在探讨人们都在做些什么？

sentences.zh: 所以我们问了他们很多开放式的问题，我最近一直在重读这些回答，那批数据收集刚刚结束不久。

sentences.en: So I don't have a full analysis done, but as I'm reading through it,
sentences.zh: 所以我还没有做完整的分析，但在我通读的过程中，

sentences.en: Right.

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's thinking about, okay, let's take the day, let's break it up into chunks.
sentences.zh: 也就是在思考，好吧，让我们把这一天划分成几个时间段。

sentences.en: This is my portion of uninterrupted time.
sentences.zh: 这段时间是我不受打扰的时间。

sentences.en: And then we switch off and I have primary responsibility for the kids.
sentences.zh: 然后我们交替，由我主要负责照顾孩子。

sentences.en: And then we switch to the, you know, back to the other spouses and we are both working with their young kids when they're napping.
sentences.zh: 然后我们再换回，你知道的，换回另一位伴侣，等年幼的孩子们午睡时，我们两个都在工作。

sentences.en: And then some people, a lot of people were saying, you know, we're waking up earlier and going to bed later to try to make this work.
sentences.zh: 还有一些人，很多人都说，你知道的，我们起得更早，睡得更晚，以此来试着维持现状。

sentences.en: But to the extent to which that's a long-term strategy, I'm guessing not right.
sentences.zh: 但至于这能在多大程度上成为一个长期策略，我猜并不能吧。

sentences.en: I'm assuming there's going to be a lot of burnout and we have measured that in the data set.
sentences.zh: 我假设大家会精疲力竭，我们在数据集中也测量了这一点。

sentences.en: So I'm interested to see if these different strategies that people use link differently to that.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，看看人们使用的这些不同策略与这种状态之间的联系是否有所不同。

sentences.en: Um, but I think the best thing is really being proactive, not just winging it, but trying to see what you can do to feel like it's fair within
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我认为最好的办法真的是要积极主动，不要只是随性应付，而是要尝试看看你能做些什么，让这在

sentences.en: your relationship to the extent, if you both are able with flexible jobs to help with the childcare.
sentences.zh: 你们的关系中显得公平，如果你们双方的工作都足够灵活，能够分担照顾孩子的任务的话。

sentences.en: And your kids will cooperate.
sentences.zh: 而且你的孩子们也会配合。

sentences.en: So when it's mommy time, it's only mommy time.
sentences.zh: 所以当这是“妈妈时间”时，就只能是“妈妈时间”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's the other layer of it.
sentences.zh: 这是其中的另一个层面。

sentences.en: Um, um, and also just, uh, thinking about
sentences.zh: 嗯，嗯，还有就是，嗯，考虑到

sentences.en: the burnout aspect of it.
sentences.zh: 精疲力竭这方面。

sentences.en: So recognizing when you're at a point when you're about to break.
sentences.zh: 也就是当意识到自己快要崩溃的时候。

sentences.en: So saying, okay, I've got to, we've got to switch something up because I need a day just to myself.
sentences.zh: 于是说，好吧，我必须，我们必须做出改变，因为我需要有一天完全属于我自己的时间。

sentences.en: I think that's a really big thing that's getting overlooked in this pandemic is just the loss of sort of me time and the loss of ability to practice self-care.
sentences.zh: 我认为在这场疫情中，有一件被严重忽视的大事，那就是“自我时间”的丧失以及关爱自己能力的丧失。

sentences.en: And I think it's important for people to figure out the way that they can do that in the context of sheltering at home and, um, the current pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们很重要的一点是，要弄清楚如何在居家令和当前的疫情背景下做到这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Are you looking at people taking vacation time as part of this study as well?
sentences.zh: 在这项研究中，你们也会关注人们休假的情况吗？

sentences.en: That seems to be a real challenge for a lot of us.
sentences.zh: 对于我们很多人来说，这似乎是一个真正的挑战。

sentences.en: Like, why would I take time off?
sentences.zh: 比如，我为什么要休假？

sentences.en: I can't go anywhere.
sentences.zh: 我又去不了任何地方。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we did ask, um, how many, uh, PTO days people had and how many they planned on using.
sentences.zh: 所以我们确实问过，嗯，人们有多少带薪休假（PTO）天数，以及他们计划用多少。

sentences.en: And so we do have that data, but it was more in the context of using it.

sentences.zh: 我们没有问为什么。我看到很多人在开放式报告中谈论更多的是使用假期，因为他们没有其他的托儿选择，对此感到非常

sentences.en: stressed about that.

sentences.en: Um, but I, I didn't, we didn't get anything about the vacation aspect, which is really, really interesting because usually people have to have that kind of break.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但我，我没有，我们没有收集到关于度假方面的信息，这真的很、真的很让人感兴趣，因为通常人们都需要那种休息。

sentences.en: And now it's tough to figure out what you would do with that time.
sentences.zh: 而现在很难弄清楚你在那段时间里可以做些什么。

sentences.zh: 还有人认为，这场疫情可能会让女性在职场倒退好多年。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the data set that we have is all couples where both are working and both have young children at home and childcare has been disrupted.
sentences.zh: 所以我们拥有的数据集里全都是这样的夫妻：双方都在工作，家里都有年幼的孩子，而且托儿服务受到了干扰。

sentences.en: And so we have these open-ended reports that people are that about what they're doing to manage right now.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有这些开放式的报告，记录了人们为了应付目前的局面正在做的事情。

sentences.en: So it's quite a bit of description scenarios here.

sentences.zh: 作为其中的一部分，你是否发现男性和女性对工作与家庭冲突的体验有所不同？

sentences.zh: 也就是说，那些用来衡量工作与家庭冲突的问题。

sentences.en: The questions would be things like my work interferes with my family life more than I would like.
sentences.zh: 这些问题会是这样的：“我的工作对家庭生活造成的干扰比我希望的要多。”

sentences.en: And then you, you answer it on a Likert scale from strongly disagree to strongly agree.
sentences.zh: 然后你用李克特量表从“非常不同意”到“非常同意”来回答它。

sentences.en: And we found no differences there.
sentences.zh: 我们在那里没有发现任何差异。

sentences.en: But what we couldn't speak to in that data set is maybe for men and women, you know, the anchors have different meanings.
sentences.zh: 但我们在那个数据集中无法说明的是，也许对于男女来说，你知道，量表两端的含义可能不同。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it could, you know, women are so socialized to think about work family issues, I think much more than men.
sentences.zh: 所以它可能，你知道的，女性被社会化得更多地去思考工作与家庭的问题，我认为比男性要多得多。

sentences.en: And so they kind of expect to have to deal with this issue.
sentences.zh: 所以她们某种程度上预料到自己必须处理这个问题。

sentences.en: And so the same situation for a man and a woman might be appraised as just an agree on the scale for, um, a woman where it's a strongly agree for a man.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于同一个情况，一个男性和一个女性可能会有不同的评估：对女性来说可能只是量表上的“同意”，而对男性来说则是“非常同意”。

sentences.en: And you really speak to that with the nature of our data, but we're doing some follow-up research to try to disentangle it more.
sentences.zh: 你不能真正用我们的数据性质来完全说明这一点，但我们正在做一些后续研究，试图更深入地剖析它。

sentences.en: Um, one, one study we're doing is a lab study where we brought men and women, not couples, but just separately men and women that were all parents into our lab.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们正在做的一项研究是实验室研究，我们将男性和女性——不是夫妻，而是单独把身为父母的男性和女性带到我们的实验室里。

sentences.en: And they read these stories about work family conflict situations that we had based off of actual real stories we got from people in a previous study.
sentences.zh: 然后他们阅读这些关于工作与家庭冲突情境的故事，这些故事是我们根据以前研究中人们提供的真实故事改编的。

sentences.en: And then we measured their physiological reactions.
sentences.zh: 接着我们测量了他们的生理反应。

sentences.en: So we have this watch called the
sentences.zh: 所以我们戴了一种叫

sentences.en: Empatica watch, which measures your galvanic skin response and your heart rate and a couple other things, which are indications of stress.
sentences.zh: Empatica的手表，它能测量你的皮肤电反应、心率以及其他几项指标，这些都是压力的表征。

sentences.en: We also measured their cortisol levels
sentences.zh: 我们还测量了他们的皮质醇水平

sentences.en: to see if there was a physiological difference.
sentences.zh: 以看看是否存在生理差异。

sentences.en: And we didn't find anything with cortisol.
sentences.zh: 我们在皮质醇方面没有发现任何结果。

sentences.en: We're still working on analyzing the other data, but then we asked, how do you think you would feel in this situation?
sentences.zh: 我们仍在努力分析其他数据，但随后我们问：你觉得在这种情况下你会有什么感受？

sentences.en: And a variety of different emotions, like guilty, angry, irritated,
sentences.zh: 以及各种不同的情绪，比如内疚、愤怒、烦躁，

sentences.en: and by huge margin, the women reported much higher emotional reactions.
sentences.zh: 结果以巨大差距显示，女性报告的情绪反应要强烈得多。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Especially guilt.
sentences.zh: 尤其是内疚。

sentences.en: That was the one that stood out the moSt.
sentences.zh: 那是表现最突出的一点。

sentences.en: I was waiting for that.
sentences.zh: 我一直在等这个结果。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: To me, that suggests that there is it, you know, maybe they are reporting the same level of conflict, but I think that women are internalizing
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这表明——你知道的，也许她们报告的冲突程度是一样的，但我认为女性正在将它

sentences.en: it and letting it affect their wellbeing more so than men are.
sentences.zh: 内化，并让它比男性更多地影响她们的幸福感。

sentences.en: Um, but, but we need to do a little bit more research before I formally say that, but that's the follow-up stuff we're doing now is just
sentences.zh: 嗯，不过，在我正式下定论之前，我们还需要做更多的研究，但这正是我们现在正在进行的后续工作，也就是

sentences.en: to try to see, is this, is this null effect, this no difference really true, or is it sort of a coming out of the way we measure things?
sentences.zh: 试图弄清楚，这种“零效应”（即没有差异）真的是真的，还是仅仅出在我们衡量事物的方式上？

sentences.en: A few high profile companies, including Facebook and Twitter have announced that they're going to let employees continue to work at home permanently, even after
sentences.zh: 一些知名公司，包括Facebook和Twitter，已经宣布它们将允许员工在这次紧急情况结束后，

sentences.en: the end of this emergency.
sentences.zh: 继续永久在家工作。

sentences.en: Do you think we're going to see a significant permanent increase in the number of companies that offer full-time telework from now on?
sentences.zh: 你认为我们是否会看到从今以后提供全职远程办公的公司数量出现显著的永久性增长？

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我会的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think that, um, tech companies for sure, sort of at the forefront of this, but I think it's going to be the wave of the future.
sentences.zh: 我认为，嗯，科技公司绝对走在这股潮流的前沿，但我认为这将是未来的大趋势。

sentences.en: I think it's going to be the, the new normal, maybe not full-time remote work.
sentences.zh: 我认为这将是，嗯，新常态，也许不是全职远程办公。

sentences.en: I think some companies will do that, but I think a lot of companies will start to let people at least work some of the time remotely.
sentences.zh: 我认为一些公司会这样做，但我认为很多公司将开始允许人们至少在部分时间里远程工作。

sentences.en: Um, yeah, there's a lot of benefits to that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，这有很多好处。

sentences.en: Um, from the organization standpoint, I think, I think about it from a real estate standpoint, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，从组织的角度来看，我想，从房地产的角度来考虑，对吧？

sentences.en: If you have a full remote
sentences.zh: 如果你拥有完全远程的

sentences.en: workforce, you can spend a lot less money on the real estate in your central office, right?
sentences.zh: 劳动力，你就可以在总部办公室的房地产上省下不少钱，对吧？

sentences.en: You don't have to have space for everybody to work all the time.
sentences.zh: 你不需要为所有人一直工作预留空间。

sentences.en: And I think it can become a really nice recruiting tool.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这能成为一个非常好的招聘工具。

sentences.en: Um, but the downsides to it are, it does, there's some evidence to suggest when you have
sentences.zh: 嗯，但它的缺点是，确实有一些证据表明，当你拥有

sentences.en: a full-time remote workforce, it does change the dynamic of the organization and that strong
sentences.zh: 全职远程办公的员工队伍时，它确实会改变组织的动态，而强有力的

sentences.en: organizational culture and strong identification that people have with an organization is harder to get.
sentences.zh: 组织文化以及人们对组织的强烈认同感会变得更难获得。

sentences.en: So I think companies like Twitter and Facebook right now announcing that they're so big, perhaps one would hit them, but for smaller companies, I think you have to really consider
sentences.zh: 所以我认为像Twitter和Facebook现在宣布他们规模这么大，也许其中一个会受到冲击，但对于小公司来说，我认为你真的必须考虑

sentences.en: how this is going to affect your culture and your practices moving forward.
sentences.zh: 这将如何影响你未来的文化和实践。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I think the innovation question is probably legitimate as well.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为创新问题可能也是合理的。

sentences.en: If you're not sort of rubbing elbows with people on a regular basis and bumping into them in the lunchroom or the bathrooms
sentences.zh: 如果你不是经常与人们摩肩接踵，在午餐厅或洗手间里偶遇他们

sentences.en: or wherever you might serendipitously run into somebody that you work with, and you might just toss out an idea and then boom, you know, here we go.
sentences.zh: 或者无论你在哪里可能会偶然碰到一个同事，你可能只是抛出一个想法，然后砰，你知道的，我们就开始了。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全同意。

sentences.en: And I think that's the big thing that that's brought up a lot.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这是经常被提起的一件大事。

sentences.en: Um,
sentences.zh: 嗯，

sentences.en: that's why I think that a partial remote workforce is really the way to go thinking about, okay,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为部分远程办公的员工队伍真的是未来的出路，试想一下，好吧，

sentences.en: so if I work, let's say two days from home, then I can think about the tasks that are best done at
sentences.zh: 如果我工作，比方说一周两天在家，那么我可以考虑那些最适合在家完成的任务

sentences.en: home where I don't need interruption, you know, I really just need to be focused for a period of time.
sentences.zh: 在那里我不需要被打扰，你知道的，我真的只需要集中一段时间的精力。

sentences.en: And then the days when I am in the office, I can reserve for the times when we need to focus on innovation or, or other things like that.
sentences.zh: 然后我在办公室的日子，我可以留给那些我们需要专注于创新或其他类似事情的时间。

sentences.en: So I, I think there's some ways that you could combine remote work to still allow for that time of innovation, but I agree with the full-time remote work.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，有一些方法可以将远程工作结合起来，仍然为创新留出时间，但我同意全职远程工作。

sentences.en: It does add a challenge.
sentences.zh: 它确实增加了一个挑战。

sentences.en: Any other predictors for how this pandemic is going to change workplaces?
sentences.zh: 还有其他关于这场大流行将如何改变工作场所的预测吗？

sentences.en: Uh, one thing that I'm, I don't know if it's so much of a prediction as a hope, but I, as a, as a work family scholar, I think that it's been interesting because of the, uh,
sentences.zh: 呃，有一件事我，我不知道与其说是预测，不如说是期望，但我，作为一个工作家庭学者，我认为这很有趣，因为呃，

sentences.en: ubiquitous use of zoom and other technologies like that.
sentences.zh: Zoom和其他类似技术的无处不在的使用。

sentences.en: Coworkers have gotten a glimpse into each other's homes and their lives in a way that they hadn't before.
sentences.zh: 同事们以前所未有的方式得以窥见彼此的家和生活。

sentences.en: And in a lot of cases, I think they've seen children running around in the background.
sentences.zh: 在很多情况下，我认为他们看到孩子在背景里跑来跑去。

sentences.en: So what I hope this will do is, is make both managers and other employees a little bit more understanding of people with families
sentences.zh: 所以我希望这能做到的是，让管理者和其他员工对有家庭的人多一些理解

sentences.en: sort of saying, okay, this person still managed to get their job done, but look at kind of the,
sentences.zh: 有点像在说，好吧，这个人还是设法完成了他们的工作，但是看看那种，

sentences.en: the chaos they had running around behind them, you know, sort of recognizing like it is tough.
sentences.zh: 他们身后跑来跑去的混乱，你知道的，有点认识到这确实不容易。

sentences.en: It is a tough balancing act.
sentences.zh: 这是一个艰难的平衡行当。

sentences.en: And, and, and the notion that we have the ideal worker is someone who has no family and puts everything into work.
sentences.zh: 而且，我们所拥有的理想员工的概念是一个没有家庭、把一切都投入到工作中的人。

sentences.en: I'm hoping we'll start to see a little bit of the erosion of that with the understanding that, Hey, people actually are their whole self.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们能开始看到这种观念的一点点侵蚀，取而代之的是这样一种理解，即嘿，人们实际上是作为一个整体存在的。

sentences.en: There's a whole side of them outside of work that I think was exposed a little bit more during time.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们在工作之外还有很大一部分生活，这段时间这暴露得更多一些。

sentences.en: Well, this has been great, really interesting stuff, Dr. Shockley.
sentences.zh: 好了，这太棒了，非常有趣的内容，肖克利博士。

sentences.en: I'm looking forward to seeing the results of this, the National Science Foundation study that you're doing.
sentences.zh: 我很期待看到你正在做的这项美国国家科学基金会研究的结果。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And we've made it, uh, actually as part of the grant, the first thing we're going to do is publish the results for a mass media audience, not academic results.
sentences.zh: 我们已经将它，实际上作为资助的一部分，我们要做的第一件事是面向大众媒体而不是学术界发布结果。

sentences.en: So we're going to get there, those out as quick as we can, and they'll be hopefully very digestible and very actionable.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会尽我们所能把这些发布出去，希望它们非常易于理解且极具操作性。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太好了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That sounds wonderful.
sentences.zh: 听起来棒极了。

sentences.en: Well, thank you again.
sentences.zh: 好的，再次谢谢你。

sentences.en: Um, I want to say the American
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想说美国

sentences.en: Psychological Association has resources and tip sheets available on our website for help in navigating work, telework, and the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 心理学会我们的网站上提供资源和提示单，以帮助人们应对工作、远程办公和大流行。

sentences.en: So visit us at APA.org.
sentences.zh: 所以请访问我们的网站 APA.org。

sentences.en: You can also find previous episodes of
sentences.zh: 你也可以在我们的网站上找到往期的

sentences.en: Speaking of Psychology on our website at www.speakingofpsychology.org.
sentences.zh: Speaking of Psychology 播客，网址是 www.speakingofpsychology.org。

sentences.en: And you can subscribe to our podcast on Apple, Stitcher, or wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你可以在 Apple、Stitcher 或任何你获取播客的地方订阅我们的播客。

sentences.en: And while you're out there, please give us a rating.
sentences.zh: 在你收听的时候，请给我们一个评分。

sentences.zh: 如果你对未来的播客有任何意见或想法，你可以发邮件至 speakingofpsychology at APA.org。

sentences.zh: Speaking of Psychology 由李

sentences.zh: 韦纳曼（Lee Weinerman）制作。

sentences.zh: 我们的声音编辑和工程师是克里斯·孔达扬（Chris Kondayan）。

sentences.zh: 美国心理学会感谢您的收听。

sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯（Kim Mills）。
